N° 14Land-evidence registry with spatial conflict detection and on-chain integrity anchoring2026

How to use TerraGuard CM

For a farmer or a family who holds land without a title and wants a dated record of it, for a buyer who wants to know what is already claimed before paying, and for a village that wants its common land on record.

Open TerraGuard CM ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Open terraguard-cm.vercel.app on a phone. The four main actions stay at the bottom of the screen: Home, Register, Check and My land.

2

To see everything at work first, open the Demo page and press Start the tour: 18 steps through five fictional cases.

3

To record land, press Register a parcel and choose how to trace it; the easiest is to walk around it.

4

To check land, press Check land and type the code the seller gives you, or stand on the land and press the button.

5

Press Listen on any screen to hear it read aloud, and Help for the full guide.

02

Features

01

Home

Four large buttons for the four things people come to do, a three-step explanation, and a plain statement of what the platform does not do: it issues no title and is not a MINDCAF service.

STEPS

  1. Press the button that matches what you want to do
  2. Press Listen to hear the page
  3. Use More at the bottom for the other pages
02

Choose how to trace

Three ways to record the boundary, from the simplest: walk around the land with the phone, tap its corners on the map, or copy the surveyor's plan.

STEPS

  1. Open Register
  2. Pick one of the three cards
  3. Change method at any time with the link at the bottom
03

Walk around the land

A signal gauge says when the GPS is good enough. At each corner the phone collects readings for five seconds and keeps their accuracy-weighted average. The screen gives the distance to the last corner and to the first one, and draws the field with the length of each side.

STEPS

  1. Wait for Good signal
  2. Press Record this corner and stay still for 5 seconds
  3. Walk to the next corner, going around
  4. Press I went all the way round
04

Check the outline

Before saving, the server computes the area and perimeter in PostGIS, names the region, division and subdivision, and compares the outline with every parcel already on the platform. The area is also given as a picture, like a square 36 m per side, and the perimeter in walking steps.

STEPS

  1. Read the area and the place
  2. Look for the green or orange box about neighbouring land
  3. Press Correct the outline, or Yes, this is my land
05

Four questions

One question per screen, answered with a tap: what the land is used for, how it is held (inherited, family inheritance, bought, given by custom, occupied and farmed, community land), whether there is a land title, and the name of the place. The answers become the declared right and its basis.

STEPS

  1. Tap the answer that fits
  2. Type the title number only if you have one
  3. Review the summary, tick the declaration and save
06

Check before paying

Three ways in: the TerraGuard code or the title number, the phone's position while standing on the land, or a receipt or report code. Each leads to the parcel's verdict.

STEPS

  1. Type the code the seller gives you
  2. Or stand in the middle of the land and press Which land is declared here?
  3. Or point the phone camera at the QR code of a receipt
07

The traffic-light answer

Red when a dispute is open, another buyer has reserved the plot, a document was altered or boundaries disagree beyond measurement error; orange when several people claim the land, an overlap may be imprecision or no paper is on file; green otherwise. Every answer states that the platform sees only what was declared on it.

STEPS

  1. Read the colour and the reasons
  2. Do the four checks before paying
  3. Press Alert me if anything changes
08

Overlaps on the map

The parcel is shown with its neighbours; the area they share is filled in red. An overlap whose mean width stays within the combined declared precision of the two outlines is presented as possible imprecision, not as a conflict.

STEPS

  1. Open a parcel record
  2. Look for red areas on the map
  3. Open the full record for overlap areas and percentages
09

Family consent

When several heirs hold land together, a sale opened by one of them is held until each co-holder's consent is recorded with a supporting document, or a court authorisation is on file. The policy names who is missing.

STEPS

  1. Open the sale
  2. Read who has not consented yet
  3. Record a documented consent
10

Disputes and mediation

A dispute keeps every claim visible and records each stage in plain words: reported, under review, referred to a professional, resolved. Resolution requires a note naming the decision or agreement, and nothing is erased.

STEPS

  1. Open Disputes from More
  2. Read the case timeline
  3. A reviewer moves the case to its next stage
11

The guided tour

A panel walks through the application itself: for each step it signs in as the person of the story, opens the real page and circles the element it describes. It can read each step aloud.

STEPS

  1. Open Demo and press Start the tour
  2. Press Next to move on
  3. Tick Read each step aloud to listen
12

Five stories

Yaoundé: a field walked on foot and a neighbour's overlapping outline. Douala: a reserved plot and a blocked second sale. Kribi: village land and a company's declared zone, about a hectare in dispute. Bafoussam: three heirs and a sale held for consent. Ngaoundéré: a field and a transhumance corridor, settled by mediation.

STEPS

  1. Press See this story under a town
  2. Follow the panel step by step
13

The book

La terre et la preuve, 302 pages in French on land rights in Cameroon: from the Crown land of the colonial period to the 1974 ordinances, the anatomy of land fraud, registries elsewhere, cartography, international standards, digital fingerprints and blockchain, with sources for every chapter.

STEPS

  1. Open The book from More or the library
  2. Read online chapter by chapter
  3. Download the PDF or the EPUB
14

Help

A guide in the application covers every screen with where to find it, what it is for, the steps and the cautions, with a five-minute start and a question list. It prints and downloads as a PDF in French or English.

STEPS

  1. Press Help at the top
  2. Pick a section in the contents
  3. Download the PDF
03Tips
  • Without network, a parcel traced on foot is kept on the phone; open My land and press Send now when the network returns.
  • A phone measures within a few metres. Only a sworn surveyor performs an official boundary survey, and only the land registry confirms who owns land.
  • Green means nothing unusual was found on TerraGuard, not that the seller owns the land: do the four checks before paying.
04FAQ
Does TerraGuard give a land title?

No. Titles are issued and kept by the land registry under the 1974 ordinances. TerraGuard keeps a dated record of declarations and papers, detects conflicts between declarations and alerts the people concerned.

What goes on the blockchain?

Only salted fingerprints of documents and events, and pseudonymous keys for parcels. No name, document, coordinate or price is written on chain. A match proves a file has not changed since it was anchored, not that it is genuine.

Is the demo data real?

People, title numbers and prices are fictional and labelled as such, in a separate database. The records and anchors are real, on the Base Sepolia test network, which has no monetary value.

Can it stop a sale made elsewhere?

No. Only sales opened through the platform can be reserved and blocked. A sale concluded before a notary or between private parties outside TerraGuard is invisible to it.

Does it work without network?

Tracing on foot does: corners are recorded from the phone's GPS and the parcel is kept on the phone until it can be sent. The map tiles and the overlap check need the network.

Who sees my papers?

The rights holders of the parcel, the professionals they engage and people given a time-limited share link. Names are masked for everyone else, and every access is logged.
